name: TURKEY TAIL
blurb: THIN ZONED BRACKETS. BLOCKS SET HARD IF LEFT.

overview.v: Dried for teas and tinctures, not sold fresh. One supplement company began by foraging turkey tail and reishi for tinctures.
overview.n: Not sold fresh: general knowledge (the brackets are thin and leathery).

overview.v: Cap n Stem keeps a turkey tail strain it knows well. Vials of it (Trametes versicolor #2, #3, #5) flew to the International Space Station in a school experiment.
Medicinal claims rest mostly on test-tube studies and are unproven. Do not repeat claims you cannot source.

cultivation.v: A matting species: the grain binds hard and breaks up far less easily than chestnut.
Blocks left too long become extremely hard and difficult to break up.

timeline.v: Usually 2-3 weeks before the plate goes in the fridge. A plate poured from colonized grain covered in about 5 days.

hazards.v: Treat every medicinal claim as unproven: the evidence is mostly in vitro or in animals.

notes.v: After the space flight its cultures recovered in about 5 days, while lion's mane was only just leaving the grain.
Tinctures: hard mushrooms such as reishi and turkey tail extracted best near 1 part mushroom to 20 parts solvent in one farm's beta-glucan tests; 1 to 1 extracts poorly.
Blended into water with a cellulose binder it makes a mycelium paper that folds without cracking if dried slowly.
